title: The Week That Was (September 7-11, 2026)
subtitle: A roundup of what I wrote, read, watched, etc. over the past week.
contentHtml:
In this space on Saturdays, I do a weekly round-up of sorts: Sifting through what I wrote that you might have missed during the week, what I’ve been reading and watching myself, and some other fun things that have been going on.

Subscribe now

📝 What I did this week

Here are the things I wrote or podcasted about during the previous week, sorted in descending order by quality, popularity and/or current relevance.

  • 📊👀 If you haven’t already, check out my many trackers for football season:

    • 📈2026 NFL Odds Tracker and Elo Ratings🏈 - This now includes updates for my QB EPA leaderboard and an experimental way to track Approximate Value in-season.

    • 🎓2026 College Football Odds Tracker and QB Rankings🏈 - The odds are running and I’m updating the QB ratings I used to use in my wildly unpopular “QB U” columns, lol.

    • ⚽ 2026-27 English Premier League Tracker 📈 - Soccer also exists!

  • 🏈🕊️ The Giants, the Broncos, and the Pre-9/11 World That Disappeared Forever - On September 10, 2001, Monday Night Football served as an accidental time capsule from a reality about to change forever. Featuring the inaugural game at Invesco Field, Jessica Simpson promos, Michael Vick commercials, and Dennis Miller in the booth, the broadcast captured all of the final elements of a vanishing era.

  • 🏒 Barry Melrose Was Hockey’s Mulleted, Larger-Than-Life Ambassador - Following his passing this week at age 70, I wanted to honor Barry Melrose — the former player, coach and longtime ESPN analyst whose sharp wit, iconic look, and passion for hockey helped bring the NHL into America’s mainstream during the sport’s cable boom.

  • 🏈 The Bills and Ravens Are Running Out of Time - Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson have dominated NFL regular seasons since their twin debuts in 2018, trailing only Patrick Mahomes in total QB EPA above replacement. But with zero Super Bowl appearances between them, historical precedent warns that championship windows don’t stay open forever for teams like Buffalo and Baltimore.

  • 🏈 Mark Your Calendars: These Are the Most Important Games of the 2026 NFL Season - By measuring the leverage of each game on NFL playoff and title probabilities, we can identify which matchups carry the highest stakes for the year ahead — and I am providing subscribers a way to track those all season.

  • 🏈 The Bears Are Coming Off a Playoff Run. Yes, This Is Usually Where It Goes Wrong. - Chicago enters 2026 coming off an unexpected division title powered (in part) by a run of good luck in turnovers and close-game wins. History says teams with that profile are primed for a harsh drop-off — but QB Caleb Williams and head coach Ben Johnson also give the Bears a legit chance to beat the regression trend.

  • 🗓️ Labor Day is Basically New Year’s For Sports - While Labor Day signals the (spiritual, if not technical) end of summer, it doubles as a “New Year’s Day” of sorts for sports fans — serving as the official launch of the most crowded, high-stakes stretch on the athletic calendar, headlined by NFL kickoff week.

  • 🏁 Denny stumbled at Darlington — but don’t write him off yet - At this week, I broke down the rough Chase opener at Darlington that threatens to throw an early wrench into Denny Hamlin’s title plans. Despite the initial setback, a favorable schedule and standings cushion make it far too early to count the No. 11 car out of the championship picture.

    • 🏁🎙️ Podracing: The Darlington Incident - In this week’s , Lauletta and I talked Darlington — Christopher Bell’s breakthrough, Denny’s disappointment, and where the title Chase currently stands. Then we look ahead to Gateway, where Tyler’s one-and-done pick is designed to hold off my insurgent contest comeback.

  • 🏈▶️ Talking FOOTBALL with Neil Paine - One of my favorite writers on this platform, , was good enough to have me on his Substack to talk about the upcoming NFL season — who do we like, who are we skeptical of, and what do we think of the state of analytics in the sport at the moment?
